text:
jamal: Heads up — prepping dedicated GPU pool for an expected Q4 EU spike. Need to open quota/limit cases across three GCP accounts: project-redwood-prod, project-redwood-dedicated, project-partners. Targets: 140x A100-80GB reserved headroom, 200 static external IPs for NAT/bastions, and ENI-equivalent (alias IP ranges / routes) increases for multi-subnet warm pools. I’ll list ask items below.

sophie: Can you drop the numbers you used for the 140 figure? breakdown? :eyes:

jamal: Sure. Forecast summary: baseline steady-state 70 concurrent A100s, expected burst to 110 for 2–4 hour windows during marketing event, add 20% safety -> 140. Breakdown: 70 steady, 40 primary burst, 30 safety/headroom.

alex: Quick cost check: 140 A100s (on-demand) in eu-west1 is ~€1.1M/month. If we reserve via committed use we can shave ~35% but it’s a 1yr commit. Do we want a short-term reserved pool or mix with preemptible/interruptible fallback?

jamal: We want Dedicated pool SLA -> no preemptible for primary capacity. Fallback can be interruptible cheaper instances. Plan: reserve 100 as Dedicated committed, keep 40 as burst with fast provisioning + interruptible fallback policy.

kevin: Networking notes: GCP NAT/egress requires static EIPs on our NAT gateways. 200 external IPs request covers NAT + admin bastions + flaky partner endpoints. Also need to request increasing 'VM instances per project' and 'CPUs per region' quotas because GPU templates spawn many attached CPUs and ENIs.

ops-liaison: FYI — partner accounts may need IAM role adjustments so their automation can consume the dedicated pool. I can open internal PR for IAM changes once quotas are sorted.

jamal: Action items I will open:
- GCP support case to increase GPUs (A100 80GB) quota in eu-west1 to 160 (we ask slightly above target to allow safety while case processes).
- Request for 220 static external IPs across projects (region/global mix).
- Request for 'regional persistent disks' and 'CPUs per region' increases tied to GPU counts.
- Service quota increase for routes / alias IP ranges to allow warm pools across 4 subnets.

alex: When you file the GCP cases please include the expected timeline (Q4 event date), reference our billing account id, and attach the forecast sheet. If we can get expedited support we should pay for it.

jamal: Will do. Draft support message: ```Hello GCP Support — Redwood Inference requests quota increases in eu-west1 for production and dedicated projects. Summary: Increase A100-80GB GPUs to 160, increase static external IP quota to 220, raise CPUs per region to X, and increase alias IP ranges/routes for warm-pool subnets. This is for a time-bound capacity runway to cover Q4 marketing burst (dates: 2026-11-15 -> 2027-01-15). Our billing account: 0A1B2C3D4E. Please advise on expedited escalation. Case owner: jamal@redwood.ai. Thank you.```

sophie: Nice. Also ask for a higher quota for 'Forwarding rules' — we hit limits when creating ephemeral load balancers for per-model endpoints.

jamal: Added forwarding rules to the request.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Reminder: last time we hit quota on 2025-10-12 and had a 6hr delay while waiting on support. Tagging escalation path: cloud-accounts@redwood.ai.

kevin: Two risks to call out for the support request: 1) Regional capacity constraints for physical A100 racks (GCP may deny increase even if quota allowed), 2) EIP pool fragmentation — we need to consolidate addresses to avoid cross-project leakage. We should include fallback policy in the support case: allow allocation across neighbouring regions (eu-west4) if eu-west1 cannot fulfill.

alex: For fallback, can we set smart routing? i.e., route low-latency traffic to eu-west1 and non-latency-critical batch to eu-west4. That reduces hard requirement for all 140 to be colocated.

jamal: Good call. I'll include: primary capacity in eu-west1 (100 reserved), burst in eu-west1 (40), and fallback burst to eu-west4 (20) if needed.

ops-liaison: I’ll prep the IAM PR and include a checklist for account owners we need signed approvals from (legal for partner projects).

sophie: Any objections to opening a 12-month committed use discount for 100 GPUs to lock price? We need finance signoff but it looks like a clear win.

alex: Finance: if we do 12-month commit, ensure the commit is applied to the correct billing account (prod vs dedicated). Mistakes there are messy. I’ll sync with finance after you open the case.

jamal: Drafting cases now. I’ll post the case numbers here once submitted. Timeline: open today, request expedited support, follow up with phone escalation if no response in 2 business hours.

kevin: Also open a ticket with our cloud provider rep about physical capacity — ask for visibility into rack-level inventory for A100/H100. Helps us decide if to request a hard reservation.

jamal: Added — will ping our rep.

sophie: Example note for the case body: include sample provisioning command and expected parallel creates to justify CPU/disk quotas. e.g.:
```bash
for i in {1..140}; do gcloud compute instances create gpu-$i --zone=eu-west1-b --machine-type=n2-highmem-32 --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100-v4,count=1 --boot-disk-size=200GB &
done
wait
```
This shows parallel create concurrency needs.

jamal: Perfect — I’ll include that snippet.

infra-bot: [quota-watcher] Noted: projects with previous quota increases: project-redwood-dedicated (case 1902345), project-partners (case 1899900). Recommend linking new requests to those previous cases.

jamal: OK linking older cases. Final note: if expedited quota increase is denied, fallback plan is: scale burst with preemptible H100 in eu-west4 + autoscaler + routing policy, and delay non-critical experiments. I’ll update this thread with case IDs and escalation steps.

kevin: 👍 and add the network team to the support case CC (netops@redwood.ai).

jamal: Will do. Thanks all — I’ll post updates here. :rocket:
